note: Which of the fetched images are actually usable, decided by looking at every one of them on contact sheets. A keyword search on a photo aggregator returns nests of empty trolleys, aisles, a tram, chefs dicing potatoes and a vernier caliper; 115 images yielded 24. Recording the decision here rather than deleting the rest keeps the yield visible, so the next person knows what these queries cost.
criterion: Several distinct packaged grocery products, in one casual photograph, at a scale where packaging is legible. A cart interior is the target; a haul spread on a counter is accepted because it has the property a shelf does not, which is products piled at angles and overlapping each other rather than faced in rows.

tiers.cart: products inside a shopping cart or trolley, the exact use case
tiers.haul: a shop's worth of products on a table or counter, piled and overlapping

near_duplicates.note: Three photographs of one cart from almost the same angle. Kept deliberately: they are the only thing in this corpus resembling several looks at one scene, which is what the tracker and the multi-frame fusion exist to exploit. They must never be split across a train/test boundary.
